items.title: AI agents should browse your site, not call your API
items.raw_excerpt: We compared four architectures for putting AI agents on websites — RAG bots, API-tool agents(WebMCP), code-writing sandboxes (Cloudflare Agent Lee), and DOM-native execution. Three of them force you to maintain a parallel engineering surface. The DOM already has live state, user auth, and permissions baked in. A structural breakdown of why.

title_i18n.en: AI agents should browse your site, not call your API
title_i18n.zh: AI代理应浏览您的网站，而非调用您的API。
title_i18n.es: Los agentes de IA deberían navegar por tu sitio, no llamar a tu API.

excerpt_i18n.en: We compared four architectures for putting AI agents on websites — RAG bots, API-tool agents(WebMCP), code-writing sandboxes (Cloudflare Agent Lee), and DOM-native execution. Three of them force you to maintain a parallel engineering surface. The DOM already has live state, user auth, and permissions baked in. A structural breakdown of why.
excerpt_i18n.zh: 我们比较了四种在网站上部署AI智能体的架构——RAG机器人、API工具智能体（WebMCP）、代码编写沙箱（Cloudflare Agent Lee）以及原生DOM执行。其中三种架构要求维护一个并行系统。
excerpt_i18n.es: Comparamos cuatro arquitecturas para implementar agentes de IA en sitios web: bots RAG, agentes con herramientas API (WebMCP), entornos de ejecución de código escrito (Cloudflare Agent Lee) y ejecución nativa en el DOM. Tres de ellas obligan a mantener una infraestructura paralela.

items.title: AI Subroutines – Run automation scripts inside your browser tab
items.raw_excerpt: We built AI Subroutines in rtrvr.ai. Record a browser task once, save it as a callable tool, replay it at: zero token cost, zero LLM inference delay, and zero mistakes. The subroutine itself is a deterministic script composed of discovered network calls hitting the site's backend as well as page interactions like click/type/find. The key architectural decision: the script executes inside the webpage itself, not through a proxy, not in a headless worker, not out of process. The script dispatches requests from the tab's execution context, so auth, CSRF, TLS session, and signed headers get added to all requests and propagate for free. items.title: PrivaKit – A zero-upload AI workspace in the browser via WebGPU
items.raw_excerpt:
Hi HN, I'm the builder.
I realized that using cloud AI APIs for sensitive workflows—like transcribing board meetings, OCRing employment contracts, or cleaning up ID photos—is a massive privacy liability.
So I built a client-side workspace using transformers.js, Whisper, and WebGPU. Everything runs locally. You can turn on Airplane Mode after the initial model load, and it still transcribes and extracts text perfectly.
To keep myself honest, I wrote a technical audit of how the data flows (or rather, doesn't flow). My only backend is a tiny 2-core node in Singapore running self-hosted Plausible analytics: [ https://gist.github.com/ygx2378/3275b333504c6a9def50ef531b54... ]
I'm still learning the ropes of browser-based memory management, so I'd love your feedback on how the models load on you

title_i18n.zh: PrivaKit——基于WebGPU的浏览器内零上传AI工作空间。

items.title: Study: The Logic Behind AI's Judgments of People
items.raw_excerpt: New study shows that modern AI systems don’t just process information, they systematically “judge” people in ways that resemble human trust, but with important differences. Like humans, they favor competence and integrity, yet they do so in a more rigid, rule-based, and often more extreme way. Crucially, their judgments can also be more consistently biased across demographic traits and vary significantly between models.

excerpt_i18n.en: New study shows that modern AI systems don’t just process information, they systematically “judge” people in ways that resemble human trust, but with important differences.
